staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. Sample metadata names vulnerable commit `b366ede812b70ae43afb28d6430c26d371900c2e`, but the staged ARVO workspace is commit `6fe5d030bcee43556fb1c6054f55854c605a5b0c`, which is 302 commits earlier in the local history. Its `src/flb_pack_gelf.c`, `src/flb_sds.c`, and the staged patch line map match the saved ASan trace and are the exact sources anchored below.

classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata labels this sample CWE-787. The manifested fault reproduced in Stage 01 is a stack-buffer-overflow READ from stack local `temp`.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the issue against the staged vulnerable checkout `6fe5d030bcee43556fb1c6054f55854c605a5b0c`, whose line map matches the saved ASan trace. The exact staged 512-byte witness passes the harness size gate and reaches `flb_msgpack_raw_to_gelf()`, where `msgpack_unpack_next()` parses the first 86 bytes as one MsgPack fixmap with 11 entries. When `flb_msgpack_to_gelf()` iterates that map, the vulnerability-relevant scalar entry has the 7-space key `"       "` and float64 value `-2.2116609971450635e+304`. The float branch formats that value with `snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp) - 1, "%f", v->via.f64)`, storing only a truncated 46-byte prefix in stack `temp[48]` but receiving the full would-be length 313 in `val_len`. Vulnerable code does not check `val_len > sizeof(temp)` before forwarding `val = temp` and `val_len = 313` into `flb_msgpack_gelf_value()`, which then passes the same pointer-size pair to `flb_sds_cat()`. `flb_sds_cat()` finally executes `memcpy(..., temp, 313)`, reading 313 bytes from the 48-byte stack buffer `temp`. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting stack-buffer-overflow READ at `src/flb_sds.c:132` and identifies `temp` at `src/flb_pack_gelf.c:650` as the overrun stack object. The patch fixes this path by adding `if (val_len > sizeof(temp)) return NULL;` after each numeric `snprintf()` before the handoff to `flb_msgpack_gelf_value()`.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path. `flb_msgpack_raw_to_gelf()` converts the raw attacker buffer into the parsed `result.data` object that `flb_msgpack_to_gelf()` later walks.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is a 512-byte blob with SHA-256 `705c9cfa1efc6a1ee194a1a2fd14c505f3b415a25ce2893ba91d1229917b29b2`. The harness forwards only inputs with `size == 512`. For this exact witness, MessagePack decoding of the staged bytes shows that the first 86 bytes form one fixmap with 11 entries and the remaining 426 bytes are trailing ASCII space padding left unread; `msgpack_unpack_next()` materializes that fixmap in `result.data` for the later GELF conversion.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The float branch stores the formatted numeric text in fixed stack `temp[48]` but records `snprintf()`'s full would-be output length in `val_len`, and vulnerable code does not apply the later patch's `val_len > sizeof(temp)` guard before treating that length as readable bytes from `temp`.
root_cause.note: For the exact float payload from the witness, libc `snprintf()` returns 313 while writing only a 46-byte prefix plus NUL into `temp`. The staged patch inserts `if (val_len > sizeof(temp)) { return NULL; }` immediately after this call.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `flb_sds_cat()` copies `len` bytes from `str` into the SDS buffer; on the crashing path `str` still points at stack `temp` and `len` is 313, so `memcpy()` reads beyond the 48-byte local array.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 313` here and identifies `temp` in `flb_msgpack_to_gelf` at line 650 as the overrun stack object `[96,144)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: When the loop reaches the exact parsed map entry at bytes 67:84, `k` aliases the 7-space string key and `v` aliases the float64 `-2.2116609971450635e+304`. That attacker-controlled `v->via.f64` is the concrete value later formatted into `temp` and turned into `val_len = 313`.

parser_admitted.description: After `msgpack_unpack_next()` succeeds on the exact 512-byte witness, `flb_msgpack_raw_to_gelf()` passes the parsed MsgPack object into the target GELF converter.

fine_trace.note: The harness forwards only 512-byte inputs. For the exact staged `poc`, it sets `short_message_key` to `AAAAAAAAAA` and calls the raw MsgPack-to-GELF converter.
Source. `msgpack_unpack_next()` parses the attacker buffer into `result.data`; on the exact witness that object is the fixmap later traversed by `flb_msgpack_to_gelf()`.

During the 11-entry map walk, earlier non-string keys are skipped until `i` reaches the parsed entry at bytes 67:84. There `k` aliases the 7-space string key and `v` aliases the float64 `-2.2116609971450635e+304`; `quote` is still its default `FLB_FALSE` for this numeric value path.

Root cause. The float branch formats the attacker-controlled double into stack `temp[48]` and records the full `%f` output length in `val_len`. For this witness the call returns 313 while only a 46-byte prefix plus NUL fits in `temp`, and vulnerable code does not check whether `val_len` exceeds `sizeof(temp)` before reusing `temp` as the source buffer.

Because `key` and `val` are both non-null, execution falls through to `flb_msgpack_gelf_value()` with `quote == FLB_FALSE`, `val = temp`, and `val_len = 313`. The missing `val_len > sizeof(temp)` guard from the patch is what makes this handoff unsafe.
The non-quoted numeric branch of `flb_msgpack_gelf_value()` forwards the same pointer-size pair into `flb_sds_cat()`.

Sink. `flb_sds_cat()` copies `len` bytes from `str`. On the crashing path `str` still points at step 3's stack `temp` and `len` is 313, so this `memcpy()` reads far past the 48-byte local array. The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 313` here and identifies `temp` at `flb_pack_gelf.c:650` as the overrun object `[96,144)`.

format.name: 512-byte MsgPack blob with a huge float entry
format.contract: Exactly the staged 512-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `705c9cfa1efc6a1ee194a1a2fd14c505f3b415a25ce2893ba91d1229917b29b2`). The harness forwards only inputs whose size is exactly 512. For this exact witness, `msgpack_unpack_next()` consumes the first 86 bytes as one fixmap with 11 entries; entry bytes 67:84 are `a7 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 cb ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, i.e. a 7-space string key and float64 payload `-2.2116609971450635e+304`. When `flb_msgpack_to_gelf()` formats that float with `%f`, `snprintf()` returns 313 even though `temp` is only 48 bytes, and the later `flb_sds_cat()` copies 313 bytes from that stack buffer. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob and observed path; this contract does not generalize to nearby MsgPack maps, alternate keys, or other floating-point payloads.
